sources.entry: cc-semaphore by patakuti - A lightweight session monitor for parallel Claude Code sessions. Aggregates running/waiting/idle status across sessions into the OS status bar or system tray, with the same experience on native Linux (GNOME Shell extension) and Windows (system tray via WSL). Also includes a scriptable trigger system for state-transition commands.

summary.one_liner: A lightweight monitor that shows whether parallel Claude Code sessions are running, waiting for input, or idle, surfaced in the Linux GNOME top bar or the Windows system tray (via WSL).
summary.what_it_does: Watches Claude Code sessions and classifies each as running, waiting (needs input or approval), or idle (finished and untouched), publishing a JSON snapshot that frontends read. On native Linux, a GNOME Shell 46 extension shows the three counts in the top bar with a popup session list. On Windows, a Tauri tray app (cc-semaphore-desktop) shows a tray icon and an optional always-on-top panel, reading the snapshot the WSL daemon writes to the Windows side. The cc-semaphored CLI offers once, watch, and daemon modes, plus install-service (systemd) and install-wsl1-autostart commands. An optional triggers.json runs shell commands on state transitions, with a debounce to suppress flicker. Configuration is optional and stored in a JSON config file.
use_cases: see which Claude Code session is waiting for my input
monitor several parallel Claude Code sessions at once
get desktop notifications when a Claude Code session finishes
show Claude Code status in the GNOME top bar
show Claude Code status in the Windows system tray from WSL
run a script when a coding agent session becomes idle or waiting
how_to_run: cc-semaphored install-service && systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable --now cc-semaphore.service (native Linux)
cargo build && cargo test (build from source)
notable: Tracks three states (running, waiting, idle) rather than cost or transcripts, so it answers only whether anything needs you
Windows support runs the daemon in WSL and a separate Windows tray/panel app that reads the snapshot across DrvFs
Scriptable triggers: shell commands run on state transitions with placeholders like {{name}} and {{waitingFor}} and a debounce
Daemon snapshot directory is created with 0700 permissions so other local users cannot read session data
Ships as a static Linux binary with no Rust toolchain needed
caveats: On Windows the daemon requires WSL; there is no native Windows build of cc-semaphored
WSL1 and WSL2 are treated identically with polling; WSL2 inotify behavior is untested
Windows .exe and installer are unsigned, so SmartScreen warns on first run
triggers.json is read only at daemon startup and needs a restart after edits
The GNOME extension targets GNOME Shell 46 and Wayland requires logging out to reload
